context.analysis:
## Overview
[The system is a hybrid insurance claims modernization platform that gradually replaces a legacy COBOL/DB2 mainframe with a modern Azure-hosted application while ensuring zero data loss and maintaining the legacy system of record.]

## Key Elements
* End Customers & Brokers (Users submitting claims online)
* Claims Adjusters (Users managing claims via the new web application)
* Operations & Finance Teams (Users monitoring regulatory compliance and consistency)
* Azure App Service (Hosting the modern claims web application and APIs)
* Azure SQL Database (Storing migrated claim types and operational data)
* Azure App Configuration (Managing feature flags for the 1-day fallback requirement)
* Azure Key Vault (Securing credentials, secrets, and customer-managed keys)
* Azure API Gateway (Validating and rate-limiting traffic to protect legacy interfaces)
* Azure Application Insights (Providing end-to-end distributed tracing across the hybrid boundary)
* On-Premises COBOL/DB2 Mainframe (System of record during the 3-year migration)

## Relationships
* End Customers & Brokers interact with Azure App Service via HTTPS/TLS 1.3 for online claim submission (R-01)
* Claims Adjusters interact with Azure App Service via HTTPS/TLS 1.3 for claim handling (R-02)
* Azure App Service communicates with Azure SQL Database via TCP/TLS for transactional data storage
* Azure App Service connects to the On-Premises COBOL/DB2 Mainframe via mTLS over a hybrid VPN/ExpressRoute for legacy claim processing
* Azure API Gateway intercepts and secures integration traffic routed to the On-Premises Mainframe interface
* Azure App Service authenticates users against Azure AD (Entra ID) using OpenID Connect (OIDC) (R-07)

## Technology Stack
* Microsoft Azure Platform (Managed PaaS selected to mitigate low team cloud experience)
* Azure App Service & Azure SQL Database (Managed hosting and relational storage to minimize operational overhead)
* Azure App Configuration & Feature Flags (Enables instant claim-type traffic toggling for the 1-day rollback requirement)
* Azure Key Vault & Managed Identities (Eliminates static credentials and secures cross-service authentication)
* Azure Application Insights (Provides distributed tracing to isolate hybrid performance bottlenecks)
* OpenID Connect (OIDC) & Azure AD / Entra ID (Secures single sign-on and multi-factor authentication)
* mTLS and API Gateway (Secures data in transit and protects the legacy mainframe interface)

## Rationale
[This hybrid architecture mitigates risk by keeping the 30-year-old mainframe as the system of record while incrementally migrating claim types to a managed Azure PaaS environment. It leverages managed services and feature flags to bridge the team's cloud skill gap, guarantee strict performance and consistency constraints, and enable rapid 1-day rollbacks if needed.]

containers.analysis:
## Overview
[The system is a hybrid cloud insurance claims modernization platform that gradually replaces a legacy on-premises mainframe while maintaining continuous claim processing. Its core purpose is to enable online customer submissions and fast adjuster workflows through an incremental strangler-fig migration.]

## Key Elements
- End Customers & Brokers
- Claims Adjusters
- Operations & Finance Teams
- On-Premises COBOL/DB2 Mainframe (System of Record)
- Azure API Gateway / Integration Container (Anti-Corruption Layer)
- Customer & Broker Portal Container
- Adjuster Workspace Container & Backend-For-Frontend (BFF)
- Azure Container Apps (ACA) / Managed Kubernetes (AKS)
- Azure Cache for Redis (PaaS)
- Azure Key Vault

## Relationships
- Customers/Brokers interact with Customer & Broker Portal via HTTPS/TLS 1.3
- Adjusters interact with Adjuster Workspace Container via HTTPS/TLS 1.3
- API Gateway routes requests to internal microservices via internal Azure Virtual Networks (VNets)
- API Gateway communicates with On-Premises COBOL/DB2 Mainframe via mTLS and TLS 1.3
- Adjuster Workspace BFF queries Azure Cache for Redis (PaaS) for read-heavy caching and session state
- Azure Container Apps authenticate to Azure Key Vault and databases using Azure Managed Identities

## Technology Stack
- Azure Container Apps (ACA) / Managed Kubernetes (AKS): Container runtime providing managed PaaS to mitigate low cloud experience
- Azure API Gateway: Manages hybrid routing, OAuth 2.0 / OIDC authentication, and the strangler fig pattern
- Azure Cache for Redis (PaaS): Offloads session state and caching to meet the <2s adjuster screen latency requirement
- Azure AD / Entra ID: Federates with on-premises Active Directory for Single Sign-On (SSO)
- GitOps (GitHub Actions / ArgoCD) & IaC: Automates deployments and eliminates configuration drift
- OpenTelemetry & Prometheus: Centralized observability stack spanning Azure and on-prem boundaries

## Rationale
[This hybrid architecture satisfies strict business constraints by isolating the expensive, slow on-premises mainframe behind an integration and caching layer. It protects data consistency and ensures low-latency user experiences while incrementally migrating claim types over three years.]

Azure API Gateway / Integration Containe.analysis:
## Overview
[The system modernizes a 30-year-old mainframe claims system through a hybrid cloud architecture, gradually migrating claim types while maintaining continuous operations. It provides a modern web interface for adjusters and online submission portals for customers and brokers.]

## Key Elements
* End Customers & Brokers
* Claims Adjusters
* Operations & Finance Teams
* On-Premises COBOL/DB2 Mainframe
* Azure API Gateway / Integration Container
* Customer & Broker Portal Container (Azure Container Apps / AKS)
* Adjuster Workspace Container & BFF (Azure Container Apps / AKS)
* Azure Cache for Redis
* Azure Key Vault

## Relationships
* End Customers & Brokers -> Azure API Gateway / Integration Container [HTTPS]
* Claims Adjusters -> Azure API Gateway / Integration Container [HTTPS]
* Operations & Finance Teams -> Azure API Gateway / Integration Container [HTTPS]
* Customer & Broker Portal Container -> Azure API Gateway / Integration Container [Internal Azure VNets]
* Adjuster Workspace Container & BFF -> Azure API Gateway / Integration Container [Internal Azure VNets]
* Azure API Gateway / Integration Container -> On-Premises COBOL/DB2 Mainframe [mTLS and TLS 1.3]

## Technology Stack
* Azure API Gateway: Acts as an Anti-Corruption Layer, OAuth 2.0 / OIDC enforcement point, and strangler fig router for hybrid claim migration.
* Azure Container Apps (ACA) / Managed Kubernetes (AKS): Hosts modern microservices for portals and adjuster workspaces to bridge the team's cloud skill gap.
* Azure Cache for Redis: Provides response caching with encrypted payloads to optimize latency and isolate mainframe bottlenecks.
* Azure Key Vault: Secures and programmatically injects cryptographic keys, mTLS certificates, and secrets via managed identities.
* Infrastructure as Code (Bicep/Terraform): Automates deployments and enforces Git-based configuration for network resilience and rollback safety.

## Rationale
[The hybrid architecture utilizes an API Gateway as an Anti-Corruption Layer to route traffic and execute the strangler fig pattern, enabling gradual claim migration without extending the rigid mainframe batch window. This design satisfies strict security, performance, and maintainability requirements while mitigating the team's limited cloud experience.]

Customer & Broker Portal Container.analysis:
## Overview
[The Customer & Broker Portal Container provides online claim submissions, self-service tracking, and draft persistence for external users. It acts as the modern digital entry point within a hybrid cloud architecture, interfacing with the on-premises legacy mainframe.]

## Key Elements
* End Customers & Brokers (Primary Users)
* Customer & Broker Portal Container (Azure Container Apps / ACA)
* Azure Service Bus (Asynchronous Queue)
* Azure Cache for Redis (Draft Persistence & Session Cache)
* Azure API Gateway / Integration Container
* Azure Key Vault (Secrets Management)

## Relationships
* End Customers & Brokers -> Customer & Broker Portal Container: Submit claims and manage drafts [HTTPS / TLS 1.3, OAuth 2.0 / OIDC]
* Customer & Broker Portal Container -> Azure Service Bus: Asynchronously queue claim submissions [AMQP / Azure Managed Identities]
* Customer & Broker Portal Container -> Azure Cache for Redis: Store temporary claim drafts and session tokens [TLS 1.3 / VNet Integration]
* Customer & Broker Portal Container -> Azure API Gateway / Integration Container: Route requests to internal microservices [Internal Azure VNets]
* Customer & Broker Portal Container -> Azure Key Vault: Retrieve cryptographic secrets [Azure Managed Identities]

## Technology Stack
* Azure Container Apps (ACA): Chosen to host the portal container due to low team cloud experience and built-in KEDA auto-scaling.
* Azure Service Bus: Implements asynchronous queuing to decouple portal submissions from legacy mainframe latency.
* Azure Cache for Redis: Provides secure, isolated ephemeral storage for user drafts and session persistence.
* OAuth 2.0 / OIDC with Azure AD (Entra ID): Enforces secure Single Sign-On and MFA for brokers and customers.

## Rationale
[Asynchronous queuing and caching isolate the modern portal from legacy mainframe latency while ensuring zero claim loss. Furthermore, managed Azure services minimize operational overhead for a team with limited cloud experience.]

Adjuster Workspace Container & Backend-F.analysis:
## Overview
This architecture summary outlines the modern cloud-native Adjuster Workspace Backend-For-Frontend (BFF) for the hybrid Insurance Claims Modernization platform. It enables rapid adjuster workflows while maintaining seamless integration with the legacy on-premises mainframe during the 3-year migration.

## Key Elements
- Claims Adjusters (Primary Users)
- Adjuster Workspace Container & BFF (Azure Container Apps)
- Azure Cache for Redis (PaaS)
- Azure API Gateway / Integration Container
- Azure Key Vault
- Azure Application Insights / Azure Monitor
- Azure Storage (WORM-enabled for audit logs)

## Relationships
- Claims Adjusters -> Adjuster Workspace Container & BFF: Manage claims via web interface [HTTPS/TLS 1.3]
- Adjuster Workspace Container & BFF -> Azure API Gateway / Integration Container: Routes microservice requests [Internal Azure VNets]
- Adjuster Workspace Container & BFF -> Azure Cache for Redis: Reads cached claim states and session data [Redis Protocol over TLS]
- Adjuster Workspace Container & BFF -> Azure Key Vault: Retrieves secrets and credentials [Azure Managed Identities]
- Adjuster Workspace Container & BFF -> Azure Storage: Streams tamper-evident audit logs [HTTPS/TLS 1.3]

## Technology Stack
- Azure Container Apps (ACA): Provides serverless container orchestration to minimize Kubernetes management complexity for a cloud-inexperienced team.
- Azure Cache for Redis: Delivers high-performance data caching to meet sub-2-second adjuster screen load requirements despite slow mainframe responses.
- Azure Active Directory / Entra ID: Enforces OpenID Connect (OIDC) Single Sign-On and RBAC at the BFF boundary.
- Azure Application Insights: Enables end-to-end distributed tracing and health monitoring across hybrid on-prem and cloud boundaries.
- Azure DevOps / GitHub Actions: Automates deployment pipelines and rollback triggers for rapid R-06 switchbacks.

## Rationale
The architecture decouples the modern adjuster workspace from legacy performance bottlenecks using caching and circuit breakers, strictly ensuring sub-2-second response times. Furthermore, it embeds enterprise-grade security, WORM audit logging, and managed cloud services to protect sensitive PII while mitigating operational risks for a team with limited cloud experience.

Azure Cache for Redis.analysis:
## Overview
The system is a hybrid insurance claims modernization platform that gradually replaces a 30-year-old on-premises mainframe while maintaining business continuity. Its core purpose is to deliver high-performance adjuster workflows and online claims processing while keeping the legacy mainframe as the system of record.

## Key Elements
* End Customers & Brokers (Users)
* Claims Adjusters (Users)
* On-Premises COBOL/DB2 Mainframe (External System)
* Azure API Gateway / Integration Container (Container)
* Customer & Broker Portal Container (Container)
* Adjuster Workspace Container & BFF (Container)
* Azure Cache for Redis Premium Tier (Container / PaaS)
* Azure Key Vault (Container / PaaS)

## Relationships
* Customer & Brokers -> Azure API Gateway: Online claim submission [HTTPS / REST]
* Claims Adjusters -> Azure API Gateway: Handle claims in web application [HTTPS / REST]
* Adjuster Workspace Container & BFF -> Azure Cache for Redis: Queries for read-heavy caching and session state [Redis Protocol]
* Adjuster Workspace Container & BFF -> On-Premises COBOL/DB2 Mainframe: Fallback claims data retrieval [SNA / MQ / HTTPS]
* Azure Services -> Azure Key Vault: Secret and access key management [HTTPS / Azure SDK]

## Technology Stack
* Azure Cache for Redis (Premium Tier): Offloads session states and reference data to achieve sub-2s screen loads while protecting the mainframe.
* Azure Container Apps (ACA) / Managed Kubernetes (AKS): Hosts modern containerized microservices and backend-for-frontend components.
* Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD): Handles single sign-on (SSO) and RBAC data plane authentication.
* Terraform / Bicep: Deploys infrastructure as code to compensate for limited cloud experience.
* Azure Private Endpoints: Secures network traffic and isolates the Redis cache.

## Rationale
This hybrid architecture isolates the fragile legacy mainframe while introducing modern caching layers to meet stringent performance and consistency requirements. It leverages managed cloud services and infrastructure-as-code to mitigate the team's limited cloud experience.
